summary.text: Joey Cohen-Saban, the Democratic and Fight Anti-Semitism Party candidate, won the election for New York State Assembly District 45 on November 3, 2026, defeating Republican Assembly Member Michael Novakhov, and is set to take office when the new term begins.
A Brooklyn native, he is a Brooklyn Democratic Party district leader and chief of staff to State Senator Sam Sutton, according to his campaign website.
He lost to Novakhov by 232 votes in 2024 and had not held elected office before this race.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, Cohen-Saban was born and raised in South Brooklyn, the son of immigrants, and grew up in Midwood and Gravesend.

He attended the Yeshivah of Flatbush and earned a degree from George Washington University, where he says he led campus campaigns on combating antisemitism, supporting survivors of sexual violence, interfaith collaboration, and the US-Israel relationship.

Cohen-Saban serves as a Brooklyn Democratic Party district leader and as chief of staff to State Senator Sam Sutton, per his campaign website, and describes himself as a board member of the Sephardic Community Federation.
He ran for this Assembly seat in 2024 as the Democratic nominee and lost to Novakhov, 49.4% to 50.2%.
He lives on the block where he grew up with his wife Florence and their two children, according to his campaign website.

He defeated Republican Assembly Member Michael Novakhov in the November 3, 2026 general election with 62% of the vote, according to unofficial results from the city Board of Elections as reported by City & State.
